source: City of Buffalo DPW Winter Snow Plan 2026-27 (Docs/sources/Buffalo_Winter_Snow_Plan_2026-27.pdf): Exhibit 'Citywide Primary/Secondary Designations' pp. 26-33 (full table in data/city_ps_table.json); operating rules pp. 8-9, 12, 16.
published_rules: Snow fleet vehicles are assigned to pre-determined routes within their specific plowing district (p. 8).
Equipment may be reassigned if some areas experience a heavier or lighter rate or depth of snowfall (p. 9).
Initial focus on primaries and secondaries (which include NFTA bus routes) and streets surrounding critical City services and life-saving facilities; then residential streets (pp. 12, 16).
Goal: at least one plow pass on every residential street within 24 hours after the snow event ends (pp. 12, 16).
limitations: Corridor streets are matched to the City's table by normalized street name; the printed limits of every matched entry span the corridor portion (e.g. Main St: S Park Ave to Bailey Ave; Grider St: E Delavan Ave to Leroy Ave).
Pre-determined district routes, turn-by-turn route order and plow districts (pp. 35-49) are not modeled; within a tier the baseline serves the nearest segment.
Humboldt Pkwy and Laurel St do not appear in the table and are treated as residential priority.

Facility access uses geocoded hospitals, police and fire stations from the plan within 200 m of a segment (data/critical_facilities.json); warming centers are not listed with addresses and are not modeled.
